_comment: TARGET-tier). One per crustify invocation target. It names the files the
target covers and in which scope, plus a target-local refinement of what
is out of scope. Values below illustrate a run scoped to ssl/statem
inside an openssl checkout; substitute for other projects.
_comment_layout: All crustify artifacts live under a single `crustify/` directory at the
repository root (which also marks the root). REPO-ROOT-tier artifacts are
TARGET-tier artifacts live under crustify/targets/<target>/ and are
invocation-scoped: this scope-config.json, the derived scope.json, and
The repo root and the target id are CLI positionals
under `crustify/targets/<target>/` records the target. Neither is
restated here: a second copy can only drift from the invocation.
_comment_files: The target's file sets, keyed by section. Repo-root-relative, always
explicit - there is no implicit directory walk. Entries are either:
* a FILE      - `include/internal/statem.h`
* a DIRECTORY, written with a trailing slash - `ssl/` - which expands
to every source/header file beneath it
`out_of_scope.paths` applies to whatever a directory entry expands to.
Naming a file the build never compiled is harmless: scope.json is anchored
on the T1 tables, so uncompiled candidates simply drop out.
THE TWO KEYS ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE. They pick the campaign:
`target`  what this target OWNS. Classification is DEFINITION-anchored:
an entity is in the target iff its BODY lives in a named file
(or, having no body, all its declarations do). Everything those
entities REACH but that is not named is derived automatically
into the sibling `import` section. Name the implementations AND
the headers that define the types - headers outside the target
tree are never discovered, and a header-only list would drop
every function it merely declares.
`import`  an API to WRAP, with nothing owned. The target section composes
empty and the import section is seeded off these files directly,
on DECLARATION-site membership - the right test for a public
header, whose declared bodies live in files this campaign does
not own. This is how you wrap a whole library.
Everything follows from that choice, with no per-item flag: a struct DEFINED
in a named file keeps its full field layout (its fields are the API), one
merely forward-declared stays an opaque handle; an owned symbol orders on its
body's callees, an imported one only on its signature. So `--transitive` over
an opaque type pulls the type and nothing else.
Scope says what the target CONTAINS, never what will be done with it: port
or wrap is the translate stage's objective, chosen per wave by the
orchestrator. Narrowing to an API SURFACE is a SELECTION concern
(`translate --file include/openssl/ssl.h`).
Ownership analysis is unaffected either way: ptr_args/ptr_ret come from the
T2 tables, which cover the whole database regardless of scope.
_comment_out_of_scope: Target-local refinement of what crustify must NOT analyze. `paths` lists
repo-root-relative paths (directories with trailing `/` recurse; entries
without are exact-file matches) that the composer skips while expanding
`files`, even when a directory entry there covers them. Project-wide
exclusions (e.g. `apps/`, `fuzz/`) are implicit via not being named in
`files` - list them here only if a directory entry would otherwise pull
them in. `features` lists macro feature names (typically
`OPENSSL_NO_<FEATURE>` or equivalent) the user wants treated as
disabled. NOTE: like `build.json`'s `features` block, this list is
currently DOCUMENTATION ONLY - no composer reads it. Dead code is
filtered implicitly instead: scope.json is anchored on the T1 tables, so
